I ran a quick sim against the sample profile (2k DAU, 2 msgs/day, 20% embeddings). Key numbers below — conservative / expected / optimistic scenarios:

- Avg tokens per message (chat): conservative 1,200 / expected 850 / optimistic 600
- Avg tokens per embedding call: conservative 1,100 / expected 900 / optimistic 700
- Per-DAU tokens/month: conservative 144k / expected 102k / optimistic 72k (derived from avg messages * averages)
- Cache hit-rate (prefix + intent cache) by endpoint: chat 25% / embeddings 10% (healthcare content is often unique so low embedding cache).
- Batching factor (practical at 100ms target): small-batch config = 4 concurrent requests, effective throughput +12% token-efficiency; relaxed batch (250ms) = factor 8, +24% efficiency but misses the 100ms latency target.
- Tokens per $ (hosted, default model): conservative ~4.2M tokens/$ / expected ~5.8M tokens/$ / optimistic ~8.0M tokens/$. For a dedicated quantized variant we see ~18-25M tokens/$.

Attached a CSV with the sim output (batching-sim-aug2.csv). Notes: these are estimates — we'll flag the assumptions in the MAP. If VitalHealth can tolerate 150–200ms P95 on conversational endpoints they can gain materially from larger batching.

Ben
Sr. Performance Engineer, Redwood Inference
